clusterBasis: Independent C review of the isolated l4-conflicts20 input and its UID-free ACTIVE vocabulary and polynomial boundary authority. Definitions contain no item identifiers.
activeTemplatePolicy: No exact ACTIVE templateKey in the supplied vocabulary matches these H1 polynomial skeletons; use null rather than borrow a cross-domain or merely adjacent template.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Use a transformed linear-divisor remainder to obtain a value of the polynomial at a point; represent the given factor-divisible difference using degree and leading-coefficient constraints; solve its remaining coefficient and evaluate the target value.
clusters.variationPolicy: Different constants, factor roots, and target evaluation points are parameter changes within this skeleton.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Use one reusable L4 for this factor-structure plus point-value parameter method.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Identify the divisor's linear factor roots and transfer known polynomial/remainder values to the low-degree remainder at those roots; evaluate directly when the target is one of the known roots, otherwise reconstruct the low-degree remainder from the root values and evaluate at the target.
clusters.variationPolicy: The divisor degree, root values, and whether interpolation is needed are input-condition variations of one root-value remainder method.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Do not split off direct evaluation or interpolation variants when the same divisor-root congruence determines the requested remainder value.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: For odd n, factor x^n+1 by x+1 to write the alternating quotient; use the divisor root for the remainder, then evaluate the quotient at that root by counting its terms.
clusters.variationPolicy: The odd exponent and the resulting number of terms are numeric parameters.
clusters.noSeparateRule: One exponent-parameterized L4 covers all odd powers divided by x+1.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Use known roots to fix coefficients, factor the resulting polynomial, enumerate every factor allocation satisfying the printed degree, leading-coefficient, and relation conditions—including allowable unit/scalar allocations—and compare the requested factor values before claiming uniqueness.
clusters.variationPolicy: Root values and stated factor relations vary; degree and normalization restrictions must be checked item by item because omissions can change uniqueness.
clusters.noSeparateRule: A single factor-assignment uniqueness L4 covers the cases; an omitted restriction is an item-level HOLD issue, not a new template.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Use a known linear factor/root condition to solve an unknown coefficient; divide by the requested linear factor to obtain its quotient, then evaluate that quotient at the specified point (including coefficient sum as evaluation at 1 only when wording is unambiguous).
clusters.variationPolicy: The linear root, coefficients, quotient variable, and requested evaluation point vary; the quotient-evaluation chain stays the same.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Use one L4 for factor-forced parameter recovery followed by quotient evaluation.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Write the original division identity; multiply by the required power, reduce the resulting numerator modulo the new product divisor, identify its degree-bounded remainder, and evaluate that remainder at the requested point.
clusters.variationPolicy: The parameter in x−a and constant remainder are symbolic inputs.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Keep this product-divisor transformation as one distinct reusable L4.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Translate each linear-divisor remainder or zero condition into a polynomial value at its divisor root; solve the resulting coefficient equations, then compute the requested coefficient expression or another linear-divisor remainder.
clusters.variationPolicy: The number of point conditions, point values, coefficient names, and final scalar expression vary while the point-evaluation system is unchanged.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Do not create separate L4s for one versus several linear point conditions or for different requested scalar combinations.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Express the polynomial as a repeated-factor divisor times its degree-bounded quotient plus the stated remainder; apply additional root conditions to determine quotient coefficients and evaluate the completed polynomial at the target.
clusters.variationPolicy: Numerical roots and remainder coefficients vary without changing the repeated-factor division identity.
clusters.noSeparateRule: One reusable skeleton covers a repeated linear factor with a linear quotient and point constraints.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Use the quotient–remainder identity for a quadratic divisor; evaluate it at the divisor's roots to determine unknown dividend coefficients, then evaluate the identity at the requested point to obtain the quotient value.
clusters.variationPolicy: The quadratic roots, parameter values, and target quotient point are numeric inputs.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Keep the root-evaluation plus target quotient evaluation chain as one distinct L4.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Write two linear division identities for the same polynomial with different remainders; evaluate both at the target root, add the resulting quotient values so the unknown polynomial value cancels, and read the sum as the requested linear-divisor remainder.
clusters.variationPolicy: Divisor roots, remainders, and the shared evaluation point vary parametrically.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Use one L4 for parallel division identities whose point-evaluated quotient values are combined.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Translate an inner linear-divisor remainder into a quotient value; substitute that value into the outer division identity at the target divisor root to obtain the requested remainder.
clusters.variationPolicy: The two linear divisor roots and remainder constants vary without changing the nested evaluation chain.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Keep nested quotient/remainder evaluation separate from parallel-quotient cancellation because the dependency structure differs.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Convert equal remainders for distinct linear divisors into equal point values and hence a product-factor form; substitute a nonreal root condition, reduce powers using its minimal polynomial, equate real coefficients, and evaluate at the requested divisor root.
clusters.variationPolicy: The specific conjugate root and numeric coefficients are inputs; the equal-remainder/product-form and real coefficient comparison remain fixed.
clusters.noSeparateRule: This complex-root constraint combined with equal linear remainders is a distinct reusable L4 skeleton.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Evaluate the product remainder at its linear divisor root; use the polynomial relation to reduce it to a square equation, enumerate both real sign branches, transfer them to the target linear remainder, and select the requested extremum.
clusters.variationPolicy: The divisor roots and scalar multipliers vary; the ± branches and extremum selection are structural.
clusters.noSeparateRule: One reusable L4 covers sign-branch values followed by a minimum or maximum selection.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Combine the sum and difference polynomial identities to determine both polynomials; evaluate each at the root of the product's linear divisor and multiply the values.
clusters.variationPolicy: The identity coefficients and divisor root vary numerically.
clusters.noSeparateRule: This identity-reconstruction followed by a product evaluation is a distinct reusable L4 skeleton.
